article.title: Asking for and giving directions
article.description: Asking: 'Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?' Giving: 'Go straight for two blocks, then turn left. It'll be on your right.' Common mistake: learners often say 'How can I go to...' instead of the more natural 'How do I get to...' or 'How can I get to...'.
article.content: Asking: 'Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?' Giving: 'Go straight for two blocks, then turn left. It'll be on your right.' Common mistake: learners often say 'How can I go to...' instead of the more natural 'How do I get to...' or 'How can I get to...'.

generated.caption: Lost and need directions? 🗺️ Many learners say "How can I go to..." but the more natural way is "How do I get to..." or "How can I get to...". For example: "Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?" Keep it natural! Save this for later & follow @EnglishVault for daily English lessons.
generated.script:
Aapne bhi kabhi ye mistake kiya hoga jab directions poochte ho?
Jab hum kisi se directions poochte hain, like 'station kaise jaana hai?', toh most people say 'How can I go to the station?'. But ye common mistake hai! The correct and natural way is 'How do I get to...' or 'How can I get to...'. Iska matlab hai, uss jagah tak kaise pahunche. For example: 'Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?' Yeh wala sentence bilkul correct hai. Samjha?
Toh ab se, jab bhi directions poochne hon, use 'How do I get to...' or 'How can I get to...'. Ab clear ho gaya na?

slides.headlineRest: — The Natural Way to Ask for Directions (Not 'How can I go to...')
slides.body: When asking for directions in English, it's most natural to use phrases like 'How do I get to...' or 'How can I get to...'. Many learners, however, mistakenly use 'How can I go to the station?', which while understandable, doesn't sound as fluent to native speakers. For example, you would politely ask, 'Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?' When someone gives you directions, listen for clear instructions such as 'Go straight for two blocks, then turn left. It'll be on your right.' Mastering these phrases helps you navigate conversations smoothly.
